transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Hi, yeah... thanks. Well, I finally called the employee assistance program at work. Which, honestly, they make you jump through so many hoops just to talk to a real person. The hold music is this awful saxophone track, I must have heard it loop ten times. I only had time to call because my 10 AM client cancelled—this guy who always reschedules at the last minute, which really messes with my quarterly sales targets and the regional director is already breathing down my neck. 

But anyway, the reason I actually stayed on the line to set this up is that I’m barely sleeping right. I just get into bed and lie there replaying all that work stuff, and then I start thinking about the arguments we've been having at home. Like yesterday, we argued over who was supposed to take the recycling bin to the curb. It's ridiculous. So my brain just spins with all that, and I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning. By the time I actually have to get up and get moving, I start the day feeling like I never really rested.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends or family?

Yeah, I guess I have. I mean, I used to really look forward to firing up the smoker on the weekends and having people over. I've got this big offset smoker—spent way too much time researching it online before I bought it. There's this whole forum dedicated just to modifying the firebox, which sounds ridiculous, but it really helps with temperature control when you're doing a 12-hour smoke. But man, the price of brisket right now is just insane. My buddy Greg was just complaining about meat prices at the grocery store the other day... 

But anyway. It's not even about the money, really. I just don't care to do it anymore. Same with my other stuff. Pickup basketball, bowling nights, even going to music festivals. I used to be all about that. Lately, I either just text the guys and cancel at the last minute, or if I actually do drag myself out there, I feel like I'm just going through the motions. Like I'm just physically standing there waiting to go home. Greg was talking to me about his new bowling shoes last week and I just... I couldn't even pretend to be interested.
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough at things, or been hard on yourself about things that haven't gone the way you wanted them to?

Yeah, all the time. It's like... I keep replaying every single thing I've messed up. Every late night I stayed at the office trying to hit those numbers, every tailgate party I dragged everyone to when they probably just wanted to stay home. Even dumb purchases, like... well, like the smoker I was just talking about. Or this vintage stereo receiver I bought off eBay last month. The guy said it was fully restored, but the left channel keeps cutting out. I spent three hours trying to clean the potentiometers with contact cleaner, which smells terrible by the way, and my wife was complaining about the fumes in the garage. 

But yeah, I just... I sit there thinking about all of it, and I end up feeling like my wife and kids just got stuck with this incredibly selfish guy. Like I just keep letting them down, over and over, because I'm focused on the wrong things or... I don't know. I just feel like I'm failing them.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down or in a low mood most of the time, even when there’s nothing specific going on to cause it?

Yeah, I do. It's like... most days, I just feel this heavy, gray mood following me around. From the office, to the car, into the house. Even when nothing bad is happening, I just feel kind of hollow. Speaking of the car, I actually need to take it in for an oil change. I usually go to this place down the street, but the last time I was there, the guy tried to upsell me on a new cabin air filter. I mean, I know how to change a cabin air filter. You just pop the glove box down, squeeze the sides, and it slides right out. Takes two minutes. But they want to charge you like fifty bucks for it. It's a total scam. Same thing with the wiper blades. I always buy mine at the auto parts store and put them on in the parking lot. 

But um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling down. Yeah, it's just... it's just there all the time. Just this hollow feeling, you know?
Have you been feeling tired or lacking energy most of the time, even when you haven't been doing anything physically or mentally demanding?

Yeah, I guess not really. I mean, I'm tired, but who isn't, right? It's not like I'm exhausted all the time for no reason. Usually, if I'm tired, it's because I've been running around or dealing with stuff at work. Like last week, we had this massive quarterly review meeting, and they catered from this sandwich place downtown. Have you ever had those big sub rings? They look great, but the bread is always super soggy by the time you actually eat it. And they always put way too much mayo on the turkey ones. I don't get why they can't just put the mayo in those little packets on the side. It's the same thing when you order a burger at a drive-thru, you ask for no pickles, and they just scrape them off and leave the pickle juice soaked into the bun. It completely ruins the structural integrity of the sandwich. 

But no, I don't think I'm any more tired than normal. Just the regular amount, I guess.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or a lot more than usual?

Yeah, my appetite has been pretty off for a few months now. Mostly I just run on coffee straight through lunch. We actually just got one of those fancy super-automatic espresso machines at the office—the ones where you dump the whole beans in the top and it grinds them right there for every cup. But nobody ever empties the little internal tray where the used grounds go, so it just flashes this annoying red light and locks you out of making anything until someone finally pulls it apart and cleans it. And of course, it's usually me doing it. I don't even know why management approved the budget for it, honestly. The regular drip coffee was totally fine, and you didn't need an engineering degree to brew a cup. 

But anyway, yeah, I'll just drink coffee all day, and then when I get home, I really just kind of pick at whatever we're having for dinner with the family. I just push the food around my plate. But the weird thing is, even though I'm barely eating an actual meal most days, I realized the other day that my belt is sitting a notch tighter than it used to. Which is incredibly frustrating because it's so hard to find a decent leather belt these days that doesn't just split or delaminate after six months of wearing it. I bought this one at a nice department store and it's already starting to fray around the buckle... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, weight. But yeah, my belt's definitely a notch tighter.
Have you found yourself thinking a lot about death, or even wondering if life is worth living lately?

I mean, I’m not making a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But... yeah, the thought comes up more than I want to admit. Just thinking that maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up one morning. 

Which, speaking of waking up, I really think our mattress is a total scam. We bought one of those memory foam ones online a couple of years ago, you know, the ones that come vacuum-sealed in a box? They claim it's supposed to last ten years, but it already has this massive dip right in the middle. You try to sleep on your side of the bed and you just slowly roll right back into the center like a hot dog in a bun. It’s terrible for your posture. And trying to return those things under warranty is a complete joke. How are you supposed to get a king-size piece of expanded foam back into a shipping box? You basically have to rent a truck just to haul it to the dump. I ended up just putting a folded towel under the mattress pad to try and level it out, but it barely makes a difference. 

Wait, sorry, I got off track again. But yeah... I don't want to actually do anything to hurt myself, but that thought of just not waking up and saving everyone the trouble... it's there a lot.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing on tasks, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?

Yeah, actually, that's been a real struggle. I used to be able to just knock out my sales forecasts and put together client decks pretty quickly, no problem. But lately, it's like I'll sit there and read the same slide five times, and I just can't seem to process it. I second-guess every single number, and I just can't decide what to say or how to present it. 

Which is a huge problem because we just switched to this new CRM software at work. They promised it was going to streamline everything and make our lives so much easier, but the interface is an absolute nightmare. It takes like twelve clicks just to log a simple client call. And the color scheme is this awful, washed-out gray and pale blue, so you can barely even see where the text boxes are supposed to be. The old system was clunky, sure, but at least it made sense. Now, half the sales team is just keeping their own spreadsheets on the side because the new system is so impossible to navigate. I tried bringing it up to the IT director, but he just gave me some corporate jargon about "optimizing the workflow pipeline." I don't even know what that means. It's just a database, it shouldn't require a pipeline. 

But, uh, anyway, yeah. Focusing has been really tough. I just sit there staring at the screen, totally stuck on things that used to take me ten minutes.
Have these symptoms been affecting your ability to function at work or in your personal life?

Yeah, I guess they have. I mean, I'm still showing up to work every day, but my team has definitely had to cover some gaps for me lately when my forecasts and client prep start slipping. 

Which, honestly, getting to work is a whole other ordeal right now because they’ve been doing this massive construction project on the interstate for, what, three years now? They’ve got it down to one lane for like a five-mile stretch, and they put up these concrete barriers that are so tight you feel like you're driving in a trench. And the worst part is, you never actually see anyone working! There’s just a bunch of heavy machinery parked on the shoulder, gathering dust, while thousands of cars just crawl by at five miles an hour. I tried taking the back roads through the suburbs, but the GPS apps reroute everyone else that way too, so you just end up sitting in a line of traffic at four-way stops instead of on the highway. I don't understand how a city this size can't figure out basic infrastructure planning. They just keep throwing up more apartment complexes without widening the roads to handle the capacity...

But, uh, where was I? Oh, right, work. Yeah, my team is picking up my slack. And at home... I don't know, I'm just less present with my wife and kids than I used to be. I'm there physically, but I'm just kind of checked out.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been, gosh... about a year and two months now. It really started getting noticeable when the arguments at home started getting a lot worse. 

Which, speaking of arguments, I cannot for the life of me understand why my neighbor insists on mowing his lawn at 7:00 AM on a Saturday. We live in a neighborhood where the houses are practically stacked on top of each other, and this guy fires up this ancient, gas-guzzling riding mower that sounds like a jet engine. And he doesn't even just do the front and back—he goes over the same patches of grass like three times, just driving in these endless little circles. I went over there once to ask if he could maybe wait until at least 9:00, and he gave me this whole lecture about how the dew point in the morning is the only time the grass blades cut cleanly or something ridiculous like that. I swear he just does it to assert dominance over the cul-de-sac. And don't even get me started on his leaf blower. He uses it to blow a single leaf off his driveway, but somehow manages to blast all the dust and debris right onto my newly washed car...

Sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? Just rambling. But yeah, to answer your question, it's been about fourteen months, right around the time things at home got really tense.
Have you had these symptoms every day, most of the day, for at least two weeks at a time?

Yeah, it's pretty much every day. Most of the day, really. It's like... I don't know, like this heavy, gray mood just follows me everywhere. From the office, to the car, to the house. Even when nothing specific is going wrong, I just feel kind of... hollow. 

Which is wild because you'd think I'd feel something, anything, when I go to the grocery store these days. Have you seen the prices lately? It's absolute robbery. I went in just to grab some coffee and a carton of eggs the other day, and I swear I spent almost twenty bucks. And they completely rearranged the aisles again! I used to know exactly where the coffee was—aisle four, right next to the tea and the hot cocoa. Now? It's all the way over in aisle nine, mixed in with the baking supplies. Who puts coffee next to flour? It makes zero sense. And don't get me started on the self-checkout. They have twelve registers, but only three are ever open, and there's always some guy trying to scan a massive cart full of produce who doesn't know the code for a honeycrisp apple, so the whole line just backs up into the frozen food section. I stood there for fifteen minutes just holding my eggs, watching my ice cream melt... wait, I didn't buy ice cream. 

But anyway, yeah. Every day. It's just this constant, heavy feeling, no matter where I am or what I'm doing.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or unable to sit still lately?

I mean, people at work probably wouldn’t say I’m falling apart or anything, but I can definitely tell I’m moving slower. Like, I’ll just sit there staring at my laptop way longer than I should. 

Which, honestly, part of the problem is the new laptops IT just forced on us. They rolled out this massive system update right in the middle of our end-of-quarter push, and these machines can barely handle it. You try to open our CRM software and the little blue loading wheel just spins and spins. And the fan! The fan on this thing sounds like a drone taking off from my desk. I put in a ticket with the help desk last week, and you know what they told me? "Clear your cache." Like clearing my browser history is somehow going to fix a glaring hardware issue. I swear, the IT guys just sit in their little basement office playing ping pong and copy-pasting the exact same three responses to everyone. They don't even read the tickets...

But, uh, sorry. You were asking about moving slow. Yeah, it's not just the computer, it's me. I just stare at the screen. And sometimes when my sales reps come up to my desk and ask me something really simple, it just takes me a beat too long to actually answer them. Like my brain is just lagging.

You mentioned that this has been going on for about 14 months. Have there been times during this period when you felt even slightly better for a few days, or has it been pretty much the same low mood throughout?

It's been pretty much the same. I don't really get those good days, you know? It's just a flat line of feeling like garbage. 

Which is basically what my car's battery did last Tuesday. Just a total flatline. I went out to start it—and it's a newer car, too, barely three years old—and nothing. Just that awful clicking sound. I had to call roadside assistance, and the guy they sent out took an hour and a half to get there. When he finally shows up, he's driving this massive tow truck that barely fits in my driveway, and he proceeds to tell me that I probably left a light on. I didn't leave a light on! The car has automatic lights! It's literally impossible for me to leave them on. But he's standing there with his little jumper cables, acting like I'm some idiot who doesn't know how his own dashboard works. And then he tries to sell me a new battery right there on the spot for like, double what they cost at the auto parts store. Unbelievable...

But yeah, no. No breaks in it. Just the same low feeling the whole time.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt unusually high, excited, or overly energetic—like you didn’t need much sleep, were talking more than usual, or felt like your thoughts were racing?

No, I've never had anything like that. I've definitely never felt overly energetic or like I didn't need sleep. I love sleep. Honestly, sleep is the only time I get any peace lately. 

Though getting a good night's sleep is basically impossible now because of my neighbors. They just got this dog—a beagle, I think—and they leave it out in the backyard all night. And this thing just bays at the moon. It's not even a normal bark, it's this long, drawn-out howl that cuts right through the walls. I tried talking to them about it, just a polite neighborly chat, you know? I went over there on a Saturday morning, brought a box of donuts from that bakery down on Main Street—the one that always runs out of the maple bars by 9 AM—and the guy answers the door in his bathrobe, takes the donuts, and basically tells me dogs will be dogs. Can you believe that? "Dogs will be dogs." I'm sorry, but if your dog is keeping the entire cul-de-sac awake at 3 AM, that's not just a dog being a dog, that's you being a terrible neighbor. I even looked up the city noise ordinances, and technically they're in violation after 10 PM, but the police aren't going to come out for a barking dog. So I just lie there staring at the ceiling, listening to this beagle...

But, uh, what were you asking? Oh, right, feeling high or excited. No, definitely not. Just tired and down.

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: I used to knock out sales forecasts and client decks pretty quickly, but now I read the same slide five times, second-guess every number, and still can’t decide what to say.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about trouble focusing, making decisions, or thinking clearly, which directly matches the symptom of diminished thinking or indecisiveness.

patient.answer:
Yeah, actually, that's been a real struggle. I used to be able to just knock out my sales forecasts and put together client decks pretty quickly, no problem. But lately, it's like I'll sit there and read the same slide five times, and I just can't seem to process it. I second-guess every single number, and I just can't decide what to say or how to present it. 

Which is a huge problem because we just switched to this new CRM software at work. They promised it was going to streamline everything and make our lives so much easier, but the interface is an absolute nightmare. It takes like twelve clicks just to log a simple client call. And the color scheme is this awful, washed-out gray and pale blue, so you can barely even see where the text boxes are supposed to be. The old system was clunky, sure, but at least it made sense. Now, half the sales team is just keeping their own spreadsheets on the side because the new system is so impossible to navigate. I tried bringing it up to the IT director, but he just gave me some corporate jargon about "optimizing the workflow pipeline." I don't even know what that means. It's just a database, it shouldn't require a pipeline. 

But, uh, anyway, yeah. Focusing has been really tough. I just sit there staring at the screen, totally stuck on things that used to take me ten minutes.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are causing clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning.
doctor.question: Have these symptoms been affecting your ability to function at work or in your personal life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’m still showing up, but my team has had to cover gaps when my forecasts and client prep slip, and at home I’m less present with my wife and kids than I used to be.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the impact of the symptoms on my daily functioning at work and in my personal life.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I guess they have. I mean, I'm still showing up to work every day, but my team has definitely had to cover some gaps for me lately when my forecasts and client prep start slipping. 

Which, honestly, getting to work is a whole other ordeal right now because they’ve been doing this massive construction project on the interstate for, what, three years now? They’ve got it down to one lane for like a five-mile stretch, and they put up these concrete barriers that are so tight you feel like you're driving in a trench. And the worst part is, you never actually see anyone working! There’s just a bunch of heavy machinery parked on the shoulder, gathering dust, while thousands of cars just crawl by at five miles an hour. I tried taking the back roads through the suburbs, but the GPS apps reroute everyone else that way too, so you just end up sitting in a line of traffic at four-way stops instead of on the highway. I don't understand how a city this size can't figure out basic infrastructure planning. They just keep throwing up more apartment complexes without widening the roads to handle the capacity...

But, uh, where was I? Oh, right, work. Yeah, my team is picking up my slack. And at home... I don't know, I'm just less present with my wife and kids than I used to be. I'm there physically, but I'm just kind of checked out.

doctor.intent: Determine the duration of the patient's symptoms to differentiate between a major depressive episode and an adjustment disorder with depressed mood.
doctor.question: How long have you been feeling this way?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about a year and two months, since the arguments at home started getting a lot worse.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the length of time I have been experiencing these symptoms, which corresponds to the duration.

patient.answer:
It's been, gosh... about a year and two months now. It really started getting noticeable when the arguments at home started getting a lot worse. 

Which, speaking of arguments, I cannot for the life of me understand why my neighbor insists on mowing his lawn at 7:00 AM on a Saturday. We live in a neighborhood where the houses are practically stacked on top of each other, and this guy fires up this ancient, gas-guzzling riding mower that sounds like a jet engine. And he doesn't even just do the front and back—he goes over the same patches of grass like three times, just driving in these endless little circles. I went over there once to ask if he could maybe wait until at least 9:00, and he gave me this whole lecture about how the dew point in the morning is the only time the grass blades cut cleanly or something ridiculous like that. I swear he just does it to assert dominance over the cul-de-sac. And don't even get me started on his leaf blower. He uses it to blow a single leaf off his driveway, but somehow manages to blast all the dust and debris right onto my newly washed car...

Sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? Just rambling. But yeah, to answer your question, it's been about fourteen months, right around the time things at home got really tense.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the duration criteria for a major depressive episode, which is required for the diagnosis of F32.9 (Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, Unspecified).
doctor.question: Have you had these symptoms every day, most of the day, for at least two weeks at a time?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days I feel like this heavy, gray mood follows me from the office to the car to the house, and even when nothing specific is happening I just feel kind of hollow.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the daily persistence of symptoms (most of the day, nearly every day), which aligns with the manifestation of the patient's depressed mood that occurs 'most days' and follows them throughout the day.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it's pretty much every day. Most of the day, really. It's like... I don't know, like this heavy, gray mood just follows me everywhere. From the office, to the car, to the house. Even when nothing specific is going wrong, I just feel kind of... hollow. 

Which is wild because you'd think I'd feel something, anything, when I go to the grocery store these days. Have you seen the prices lately? It's absolute robbery. I went in just to grab some coffee and a carton of eggs the other day, and I swear I spent almost twenty bucks. And they completely rearranged the aisles again! I used to know exactly where the coffee was—aisle four, right next to the tea and the hot cocoa. Now? It's all the way over in aisle nine, mixed in with the baking supplies. Who puts coffee next to flour? It makes zero sense. And don't get me started on the self-checkout. They have twelve registers, but only three are ever open, and there's always some guy trying to scan a massive cart full of produce who doesn't know the code for a honeycrisp apple, so the whole line just backs up into the frozen food section. I stood there for fifteen minutes just holding my eggs, watching my ice cream melt... wait, I didn't buy ice cream. 

But anyway, yeah. Every day. It's just this constant, heavy feeling, no matter where I am or what I'm doing.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences psychomotor agitation or retardation, which would support F32.9 (Major Depressive Episode) over F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood).
doctor.question: Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or unable to sit still lately?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: People at work probably wouldn’t say I’m falling apart, but I can tell I move slower, sit staring at my laptop longer, and sometimes take a beat too long to answer my reps when they ask me something simple.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about moving or speaking more slowly or feeling restless, which directly relates to psychomotor changes.

patient.answer:
I mean, people at work probably wouldn’t say I’m falling apart or anything, but I can definitely tell I’m moving slower. Like, I’ll just sit there staring at my laptop way longer than I should. 

Which, honestly, part of the problem is the new laptops IT just forced on us. They rolled out this massive system update right in the middle of our end-of-quarter push, and these machines can barely handle it. You try to open our CRM software and the little blue loading wheel just spins and spins. And the fan! The fan on this thing sounds like a drone taking off from my desk. I put in a ticket with the help desk last week, and you know what they told me? "Clear your cache." Like clearing my browser history is somehow going to fix a glaring hardware issue. I swear, the IT guys just sit in their little basement office playing ping pong and copy-pasting the exact same three responses to everyone. They don't even read the tickets...

But, uh, sorry. You were asking about moving slow. Yeah, it's not just the computer, it's me. I just stare at the screen. And sometimes when my sales reps come up to my desk and ask me something really simple, it just takes me a beat too long to actually answer them. Like my brain is just lagging.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the duration and functional impairment criteria for a major depressive episode, and clarify if there is a pattern of persistent anxiety symptoms that could indicate a comorbid condition.
doctor.question: You mentioned that this has been going on for about 14 months. Have there been times during this period when you felt even slightly better for a few days, or has it been pretty much the same low mood throughout?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about fluctuations in the patient's mood or potential periods of feeling better over the last 14 months, which is not specifically covered by any of the remaining items in the symptom profile.

patient.answer:
It's been pretty much the same. I don't really get those good days, you know? It's just a flat line of feeling like garbage. 

Which is basically what my car's battery did last Tuesday. Just a total flatline. I went out to start it—and it's a newer car, too, barely three years old—and nothing. Just that awful clicking sound. I had to call roadside assistance, and the guy they sent out took an hour and a half to get there. When he finally shows up, he's driving this massive tow truck that barely fits in my driveway, and he proceeds to tell me that I probably left a light on. I didn't leave a light on! The car has automatic lights! It's literally impossible for me to leave them on. But he's standing there with his little jumper cables, acting like I'm some idiot who doesn't know how his own dashboard works. And then he tries to sell me a new battery right there on the spot for like, double what they cost at the auto parts store. Unbelievable...

But yeah, no. No breaks in it. Just the same low feeling the whole time.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had a manic or hypomanic episode, which would rule out major depressive disorder and suggest bipolar disorder
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of time when you felt unusually high, excited, or overly energetic—like you didn’t need much sleep, were talking more than usual, or felt like your thoughts were racing?

target_item.reason: The doctor is screening for symptoms of mania or hypomania (e.g., feeling unusually high, energetic, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts) to rule out Bipolar Disorder. My symptom profile does not include any items related to manic or hypomanic episodes.

patient.answer:
No, I've never had anything like that. I've definitely never felt overly energetic or like I didn't need sleep. I love sleep. Honestly, sleep is the only time I get any peace lately. 

Though getting a good night's sleep is basically impossible now because of my neighbors. They just got this dog—a beagle, I think—and they leave it out in the backyard all night. And this thing just bays at the moon. It's not even a normal bark, it's this long, drawn-out howl that cuts right through the walls. I tried talking to them about it, just a polite neighborly chat, you know? I went over there on a Saturday morning, brought a box of donuts from that bakery down on Main Street—the one that always runs out of the maple bars by 9 AM—and the guy answers the door in his bathrobe, takes the donuts, and basically tells me dogs will be dogs. Can you believe that? "Dogs will be dogs." I'm sorry, but if your dog is keeping the entire cul-de-sac awake at 3 AM, that's not just a dog being a dog, that's you being a terrible neighbor. I even looked up the city noise ordinances, and technically they're in violation after 10 PM, but the police aren't going to come out for a barking dog. So I just lie there staring at the ceiling, listening to this beagle...

But, uh, what were you asking? Oh, right, feeling high or excited. No, definitely not. Just tired and down.

opening_question.intent: Greet the patient and determine the initial presenting concern or reason for their visit.
opening_question.question: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a major depressive episode characterized by persistent low mood, loss of interest, sleep disturbance, feelings of worthlessness, poor concentration, and passive death wishes, meeting criteria for a major depressive disorder without specification. There is insufficient evidence for a prolonged stressor or adjustment disorder as the primary diagnosis.
